sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display context confirmed (companion paper PMC9220218 uses anti-PA staining to detect surface-exposed EpCAM); exact functional assay result for the N-terminal PA-tagged full-length construct not detailed in this clip.
sites.rationale: EpCAM is a type I transmembrane protein; the signal peptide spans residues 1–23 and is cleaved co-translationally, placing the mature N-terminus (residue 24, Q) on the extracellular face. An N-terminal tag must be inserted after residue 23 (the last SP residue, A) so it is not co-cleaved with the signal peptide. Python verification confirms seq[22]='A' and seq[23]='Q', consistent with the landmarks. This is the sole extracellular terminus; the C-terminus (residue 314) is intracellular. Full-length EpCAM with an N-terminal PA tag was subcloned into a mammalian expression vector (pCAG-Ble); deletion mutants (dN44–dN244) were also produced with the same N-terminal PA tag. EpCAM is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with signal peptide 1–23 and a single extracellular N-terminus at residue 24; the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus available for tagging.

sources.claim: N-terminal PA-tagged EpCAM deletion mutants (dN44, dN64, dN84, dN104, dN124, dN144, dN164, dN184, dN204, dN224, and dN244) were produced using a HotStar HiFidelity Polymerase Kit (Qiagen Inc., Hilden, Germany), and subcloned into the pCAG-Ble vector.

literature_notes: L1 and L3 describe C-terminal PA-tagged full-length EpCAM; the C-terminus (residue 314) falls within the intracellular domain (289–314) and is therefore not a surface tag site. L4, L5, and L6 describe C-terminal GFP/EGFP fusions; these are likewise intracellular. All five C-terminal constructs are recorded in other_positions. L6 confirms that C-terminally tagged EpCAM-EGFP traffics to the cell surface (flow cytometry), validating that the ectodomain folds and traffics correctly even with a bulky C-terminal fusion, but the EGFP itself is intracellular. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop insertion for EpCAM.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal PA tag on full-length EpCAM; residue 314 (A) is in the intracellular domain (289–314), so the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
